long_biography.plain_text:
At ZAM, the district centre in Munich's Freiham neighbourhood, architect and developer Alexander Rosa-Alscher brought homes, shops, offices and restaurants together around a public square. His group worked with Stoermer Murphy and Partners on the design and with other development and construction partners to deliver the scheme.

The centre applies a fifteen-minute neighbourhood concept, placing everyday activities close together. Its residential offering ranges from furnished single-room apartments to larger family homes, while arcades connect the buildings around Mahatma-Gandhi-Platz. Rosa-Alscher hosted residents and visitors at the opening celebrations in 2024. By then, shops and restaurants in his group's completed section had secured tenants, and the first residents had moved in.
